name: Jehoiarib
title: Head of the Priestly Division
summary: Jehoiarib (also called Jehoiarib) was the head of the first of the 24 priestly divisions established by David. His descendants were among those who returned from exile in Babylon and settled in Jerusalem. The family of Jehoiarib gained great significance in later times, as the Maccabees (Hasmoneans) belonged to this priestly lineage.

keyEvents.title: Listed among the priestly divisions under David
keyEvents.description: Jehoiarib was appointed as the first of the 24 priestly divisions that served in the temple, an arrangement established by King David.

keyEvents.title: Jehoiarib mentioned among priests in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: After returning from the Babylonian exile, Jehoiarib is mentioned among the priests who settled in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Listed in Nehemiah's register of priests
keyEvents.description: Jehoiarib is mentioned among the priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel to the promised land after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Ezra seeks Levites at the river Ahava
keyEvents.description: In connection with Ezra's return, Joiarib is mentioned as one of the learned men Ezra sent for to ensure Levitical service during the journey back to Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Registration of the priestly line under Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: Joiarib is recorded in the genealogies as head of a priestly family in Nehemiah's time, confirming the family's continued significance after the exile.
